items.title: Construction of new pumping station expected to begin next week in Mississauga
items.summary: Construction is expected to begin next week on a fourth automated pumping station in a northwest Mississauga community that’s experienced severe flooding for years, the city says. With the third pumping station up and running in the Lisgar area of west Meadowvale since August, the City of Mississauga has now awarded the contract to get the long-awaited fourth facility built, Mississauga Ward 10 Coun. Sue McFadden said in an update to constituents on Thursday. The “critical” pieces of new infrastructure at Osprey Marsh will better protect people and their homes from major flooding in the city’s northwest corner, city officials have said. , “with a mobilization date of Nov. ” Continuing, the councillor noted that “like the three (stations) before it, this pumping station is designed to pump water out of the Foundation Drain Collector system, creating additional capacity in the pipes to prevent backups and surcharges during large storm events or sudden extreme snow melt. “This last of the four approved stations will be located at the east end of Osprey Marsh, just south of Osprey Boulevard at Sixteen Mile Creek. It is scheduled to be operational by December 2027. ” McFadden added a construction notice has been sent to properties within close proximity of the new infrastructure.

items.title: Massage therapist from Mississauga charged with sexual assault
items.summary: A Mississauga man who worked as a registered massage therapist in Milton has been charged with sexual assault after a woman came forward to police. Halton Regional Police said they charged the man on Thursday in connection with an alleged assault that took place in May 2025 when the suspect was employed at Massage Addict on Steeles Avenue in Milton. Investigators with the Child Abuse and Sexual Assault Unit said they began looking into the complaint from the victim last month. Ayman Alkassem, 53, of Mississauga, was arrested on Nov. 19 and charged with one count of sexual assault, police said in a news release. The accused has been held in custody pending a bail hearing in Milton court. Alkassem was also charged with sexual assault in June 2025 in connection with another incident alleged to have happened at the same massage business, police said. Investigators at that time said the accused had been employed at other massage studios as well, including additional locations in Mississauga. Ayman Alkassem, 53, of Mississauga.

items.title: Suspect in Mississauga murder still sought despite dropping off Canada’s most-wanted list
items.summary: A man hunted by police in the slaying of a young woman who was killed while working at a Mississauga gas station in 2022 is still actively being pursued despite being dropped from Canada’s top 25 most-wanted fugitives list. Dharam Dhaliwal, now 33, appeared on the BOLO Program’s 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 25 Most Wanted in Canada lists, but was not included in the updated version revealed Thursday morning. The BOLO Program, which takes its name from the popular police term “be on the lookout,” leverages social media, technology and “innovative engagement” to raise awareness about wanted people and encourage citizens to be on the lookout for Canada’s most-wanted suspects. It was developed in partnership with police forces across Canada and Crime Stoppers programs and regularly — usually once a year — releases a 25 Most Wanted in Canada list. Dhaliwal, who’s being hunted by Peel Regional Police on a nationwide first-degree murder warrant, was included among Canada’s 25 most-wanted fugitives for the first time in April 2024, when he was No. 9 on the list. Later that year, he occupied the No. 15 spot and in BOLO’s late 2025 update he appeared at No. 21. Dharam Dhaliwal, 33, is wanted in connection with a December 2022 murder at a Mississauga gas station.

items.title: Mayors' Joint Affordability Appeal Shapes Peel Chair Iannicca's First Budget of New Term
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Peel Region's returning chair Nando Iannicca told newly elected regional council Thursday that affordability will top his agenda as he begins a four year term and prepares a review of regional spending for next year's budget. Iannicca was reappointed for 2026 to 2030, making him the only one of eight regional and upper tier chairs province wide to keep his seat after the election, the outlet reports. Last week the mayors of Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon jointly urged him to put reducing residents' financial burden at the centre of his first budget, according to insauga.com. Iannicca said he had heard that message and quoted their letter urging him to take the responsibility seriously. He added that he has spoken with the mayors and thanked them for pressing the point, the outlet reported. Rising living costs, he said, must guide the region's decisions.

items.title: Volunteer Group Credits a Seven-Year-Old's Persistence for Its Mississauga Litter Cleanups
items.summary: According to insauga.com, a Mississauga volunteer group called People Against Littering has held litter cleanups this year largely because of a seven year old boy named Leo who kept flagging trash in his neighbourhood. Group founder Bill Godfrey, 79, told insauga.com that Leo first joined a cleanup in Brampton in 2022 at age three, before his family moved to Mississauga two years ago. Leo's mother, Steph Costa, said her son then began spotting litter piling up near The Exchange and Burnhamthorpe Road in his new neighbourhood. Godfrey said it took the boy's attention to notice a problem he believes has existed in Mississauga for years. The group gathered at that site three times this year, according to Godfrey, and Costa said Leo remains frustrated that litter keeps returning to the same spot. Godfrey added that Leo has recently received two awards recognizing his efforts.

items.title: Warm Weather Cancels Mississauga's Outdoor Rink Opening as Santa Claus Parade Closes Downtown Roads
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, a number of downtown roads will close and parking restrictions will take effect this Saturday for the annual Santa Claus parade and the lighting of the Christmas tree at Celebration Square. City officials said closures and restrictions begin at noon along the parade route and that roads will reopen once the parade has passed through the area. The city normally opens its largest outdoor ice rink at Celebration Square as part of the festivities, but officials said recent warm weather means the rink will not open this Saturday. Officials warned residents to expect congestion and delays downtown, and said MiWay service updates and detours will also be in effect because of the parade. The city noted that closure times could change, ending earlier or later than planned, and said Peel Regional Police will reopen roads as soon as it is safe to do so.

items.title: Mississauga launches new initiative to help local businesses grow in the aerospace industry
items.summary: Creating new opportunities for local businesses through the launch of the Mississauga Aerospace & Defence Ready Accelerator program. Business and innovation | November 19, 2026 Mississauga, through Invest Mississauga, is creating new opportunities for local businesses through the launch of the Mississauga Aerospace & Defence Ready Accelerator (MADRA), a new program designed to help companies prepare for and access opportunities in Canada’s growing aerospace and defence sectors. The announcement was made at the Defence Ready Mississauga: Your Pathway into Canada’s Defence Supply Chain event on November 16 in partnership with Business Development Bank of Canada (BDC). MADRA will provide local businesses with expert guidance, industry connections and readiness assessments to help them compete for opportunities in both commercial and defence-related aerospace markets. Developed in partnership with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Canada Aerospace (MHICA), the Ontario Aerospace Council (OAC) and Downsview Aerospace Innovation & Research (DAIR), MADRA will help businesses understand industry standards, build new connections and get ready for opportunities in the commercial and military aerospace sectors. While opportunities in aerospace and defence continue to grow, many businesses face barriers to entry due to required certifications, technical requirements and the need to build relationships with established companies. Through MADRA, participating companies will receive one-on-one support from industry experts who will: The launch comes as the Government of Canada increases its focus on national defence investments and stronger Canadian supply chains. Through the federal Industrial and Technological Benefits (ITB) Policy, companies awarded major defence contracts are required to invest and do business in Canada, creating significant opportunities for Canadian suppliers, including small- and medium-sized enterprises.

items.title: Federal Housing Fund Backs $1 Million in Mississauga Rebates for Basement and Garage Conversions
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, homeowners can tap more than $1 million in funding through the city's Gentle Density Incentive Program to help cover the cost of adding new licensed units to their properties. The city says the incentives apply to units such as basement apartments, garage conversions, garden suites, triplexes and fourplexes, lowering costs for homeowners creating new housing. Mississauga reports it has issued more than $839,000 in gentle density incentives so far, funded through the federal Housing Accelerator Fund. In most cases, the city says homeowners building one or two units automatically get a rebate covering permit fees once construction is complete. The city notes homeowners building a fourplex may qualify for extra incentives, and it is promoting the program ahead of National Housing Day. The funding is available for a limited time, according to the city.

items.title: Brampton Assault Call Leads Police to Fatal Standoff at UTM Student Residence
items.summary: According to the SIU, Peel police received a 911 call Monday afternoon after a man allegedly assaulted a woman in Brampton, and officers located him later that evening at a student residence on the University of Toronto Mississauga campus near Dundas Street West and Mississauga Road. The watchdog says a gunshot was heard and the 19 year old man was found with an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound, and he was pronounced dead early Tuesday morning. Before the shooting was confirmed, UTM issued an alert telling students to shelter in place because of police activity near the McLuhan Court residence, according to the university. Ontario's Special Investigations Unit has opened an investigation into the circumstances of the death, the SIU said. UTM said Tuesday it was saddened by the death and the investigation, and confirmed the campus would stay open while cancelling Tuesday classes.

items.title: Prologis And Montcrest Challenge Mississauga’s Data Centre Freeze
items.summary: Sign up for Connect emails to stay informed with CRE stories that are 150 words or less. Prologis and Montcrest Asset Management have filed separate appeals of Mississauga’s freeze on large data centres, putting a stalled 40-MW project in Meadowvale and the future use of a property near Pearson airport before the Ontario Land Tribunal. Council adopted the freeze it proposed in July on Sept. 16. The bylaw pauses new facilities, conversions and expansions with peak power demand of 10 MW or more for up to a year. Mississauga is among the largest Canadian municipalities to impose a pause as local councils grapple with how to regulate large data centres. Neighbouring Oakville adopted its own temporary restrictions in August, and Calgary is weighing a pause of its own. Prologis wants the tribunal to overturn the bylaw. , just south of Highway 401, for a two-storey, 227K-SF data centre. Before the freeze, city planners flagged outstanding issues with servicing, stormwater management and building design. The application remains under review. Montcrest is seeking an exemption for its Tahoe Centre property near Eglinton Avenue East and Tahoe Boulevard. It says the site is already zoned for data processing and argues the city is using a land-use bylaw to regulate electricity demand. City staff expect to report to council later this year on how they’ll study where large data centres can go and what rules they should meet.

items.title: Peel Police Charge Two Men, Including an Off-Duty Sudbury Officer, After Mississauga Hotel Dispute
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police, two men were charged following an altercation at a Mississauga hotel on Nov. 7, including 40 year old Jeffrey Mussen, a sergeant with the Greater Sudbury Police Service's Intimate Partner Violence Unit who was off duty at the time. Peel police told CTV News that Mussen was charged with assault, while 48 year old Matthew Bedard was charged with uttering threats to cause death or bodily harm. Both men were released at the scene and will appear in court later, according to Peel police. Greater Sudbury Police Service spokesperson Kaitlyn Dunn told CTV News the service is aware of the charge against Mussen but said it would be inappropriate to comment since the matter is before the courts and occurred outside its jurisdiction. Sudbury police said allegations of criminal conduct involving its members go through the proper legal and internal processes.

items.title: Fergus Avenue Building Sees Extended Police Presence Over Person in Crisis
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police, officers responded to a person in crisis at an apartment building on Fergus Avenue in Mississauga on Wednesday afternoon. Police say the incident is contained to a single unit and that there is no concern for the safety of other residents in the building. The force said in a social media update that there will be an extended police presence in the area as the situation continues. Peel police are asking drivers to avoid the area and seek alternate routes if possible. Residents who are unsure whether they can access the property are being told to speak with an officer on scene for direction, according to the police bulletin.
